newsitem.title: USA: DFS holders aim to reverse sale to LVMH.
newsitem.headline: DFS holders aim to reverse sale to LVMH.

text.p: Two shareholders of DFS Group LP said on Friday they are seeking to reverse the sale of a controlling stake in the duty free store chain to LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton after an aribtrator permitted the sale.

Robert Miller and Anthony Pilaro, shareholders with a 41.25 percent stake in DFS, filed a motion with the Supreme Court of the State of New York seeking to vacate the deal that values all of DFS at approximately $4 billion with its $2.47 billion bid for a controlling stake.
Miller and Pilaro said in a statement LVMH's purchase violated a 1991 shareholder agreement between DFS holders.
Charles Feeney and Alan Parker are trying to sell their 58.75 percent stake in DFS to LVMH.

Miller and Pilaro said Ira Millstein, an independent arbitrator, did not give them the opportunity to present evidence of an inherent conflict of interest between LVMH and DFS and that he did not rule on the primary issues presented to him.
Also, Miller and Pilaro contend that Millstein improperly forced them into an unwanted contract to arbitrate with LVMH, they said.
Representatives from privately held DFS and LVMH, a maker of luxury goods including Dom Perignon champagne and Christian Dior perfumes, were not immediately available for comment.
Miller and Pilaro claimed that LVMH has changed its plans for DFS from operating it as an autonomous retailer to "bringing necessary synergies" to the enterprise.
LVMH American depository receipts (ADRs) fell 1-1/8 to 53-1/4 on volume of 14,100 ADRs.
Miller and Pilaro alleged that LVMH would show no concern for the interests of DFS minority shareholders.
Representatives from privately held DFS did not have an immediate comment. A U.S. representative for LVMH declined to comment, saying that LVMH has not yet seen the court filings.
